entries.text: Father Mikhail's Foreign Venture MOM-020 · Divided Attention Father Mikhail travels to Cardiff on special-envoy duty and is drawn into a life-and-death operation against several Magi threats. Lynleit is later sent abroad to assist him, without MSF or its conventional arsenal. Mikhail and Lynleit complete their missions while disagreeing over their methods. Cardiff, United Kingdom Father Mikhail travels to Cardiff to perform special-envoy duties for the Church. The assignment develops into a life-and-death ordeal. Mikhail faces several Magi threats alone before assistance reaches him. He survives and defeats some of those threats, establishing him as a formidable Church warrior. The venture reveals more of Mikhail's past, personality, and capabilities. The Magiarchy and Church later request Lynleit's assistance in Cardiff. Because Lynleit is abroad, she cannot rely on MSF or its conventional arsenal and must depend on her training as a Magus. Lynleit and Mikhail continue to cooperate, fulfil their missions, and protect one another. Their methods of solving the crisis are morally incompatible, and the rift between them grows during the operation. Consequences from Cardiff later enter the main story in Narvea. The Academy crisis unfolds in Narvea during Lynleit's Cardiff dispatch, dividing her responsibilities between a mission she must perform herself and a danger she has delegated to Kyrien. What special-envoy duty brings Mikhail to Cardiff, and which event turns it into a life-and-death operation? Which Magi threats does Mikhail face, and what Church techniques let him survive them alone? What part of Mikhail's past is exposed by the operation? Which specific method divides Lynleit and Mikhail morally while still requiring them to protect one another? What consequence follows them from Cardiff into Narvea? How many Chapters belong to the side story, and where do they alternate with the Academy operation? Mikhail already serves as a special envoy and has confronted Lynleit over forbidden knowledge. Natalia asks Lynleit to help Myka shortly before the foreign dispatch removes Lynleit from Narvea. Lynleit and Mikhail return from a successful but morally divisive cooperation. Helena's response is a directed hunt for Lynleit's arrest. Lynleit uses every available resource she can reach to evade capture. Her emotions surface only after she reaches safety in Kyrien's hotel room. She stays the night. There is no sexual interaction between them. Kyrien holds her while she falls asleep. Helena has used Fionn's death to frame Lynleit and direct a hunt for her arrest, forcing her to rely on the secret ally she recruited long before the danger became visible. Their bond remains non-sexual at this point, but it becomes a private source of safety within Lynleit's continuing effort to reclaim MSF. entries.text: Terrors Inside the Academy MOM-018 · Divided Attention While Lynleit is dispatched to Cardiff, she answers Natalia's request by sending Kyrien into the Magi Academy as Myka's undercover helper. The danger exceeds Lynleit's estimate and forces Natalia to intervene personally. Kyrien protects Myka until the escalating danger forces Natalia to intervene. Magi Academy Myka encounters terrors inside the Magi Academy. She relies on Natalia for rescue, advice, and support. Natalia asks Lynleit to help Myka. Natalia was Lynleit's favourite teacher during Lynleit's Magi Academy years. Lynleit cannot intervene personally because the Magiarchy and Church have dispatched her to Cardiff to assist Father Mikhail. Lynleit sends Kyrien into the Academy as a substitute undercover helper. Lynleit understates the threat and expects the assignment to help Kyrien understand the Magi world. Kyrien enters the operation as a non-Magus working inside a Magus institution. The danger Kyrien and Myka encounter exceeds Lynleit's estimate. Kyrien relies on conventional field skills and communications with Felix and Reiner to keep Myka safe. Natalia is forced to intervene personally. This is Myka's first exposure to Kyrien and MSF. The experience contributes to Myka's later decision to join MSF after graduation. What terrors does Myka encounter, and why can the Academy not resolve them through its own hierarchy? What cover, objective, and practical access allow Kyrien to operate inside the Academy? How does Kyrien communicate with Felix and Reiner without exposing the operation? Which event forces Natalia to intervene personally? How are the Academy crisis and the Cardiff venture divided across their parallel chapters? Myka already relies on Natalia for ordinary academic advice and personal reassurance. Natalia asks her former favourite student Lynleit for help shortly before Lynleit leaves for Cardiff. Surviving the Academy crisis contributes to the knowledge and strength with which Myka later graduates at the top of her class. Her first experience with Kyrien and MSF gives her a personal reason to join the agency later. Myka myka Natalia natalia Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: The Coat Fionn Left Behind
entries.subtitle: MOM-016 · Clear Her Name
entries.text: The Coat Fionn Left Behind MOM-016 · Clear Her Name Midway through Arc 1, after losing a blue suede jacket in the river and after Fionn's death, Lynleit learns that he had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wears with a garment sewn from material called the hide of leviathan. Lynleit discovers Fionn's concealed gift and learns that she cannot command its form. Unspecified Lynleit loses a fitted blue suede jacket during the Drowned Choir attack and later complains about the loss because she liked it. After Fionn's death, Lynleit discovers that he had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wears. The discovery occurs in the middle of Arc 1. The replacement is sewn from material called the hide of leviathan. The coat can shield its user from minor magically induced damage and phenomena. Wearing the coat is not enough to activate its protection. Lynleit must cover the threatened part of her body or remove the garment and place or throw it over someone who needs protection. The coat chooses its own form. It may appear as a coat, scarf, an imitation of Lynleit's lost blue jacket, or another piece of clothing. Lynleit cannot command the change, which creates occasional practical and comic problems. When did Fionn replace the original coat, and how did he do it without Lynleit noticing? How does Lynleit discover the substitution after his death? What does hide of leviathan mean, and is it connected to the river phenomenon recorded as HI-004? What counts as minor magically induced damage, and what limits the coat's protection? Why does the coat choose forms autonomously, and can it refuse the form Lynleit needs? Lynleit loses the blue suede jacket during the river operation. Fionn dies without explaining the protective garment he had placed in her wardrobe. The inherited coat becomes part of Lynleit's equipment. Its changing forms can preserve the silhouette of the lost jacket, but its protection remains deliberate rather than automatic. Lynleit lynleit Fionn fionn

entries.title: The Empty Boats Beneath the Bridge
entries.subtitle: MOM-006 · Unknowing Convergence
entries.text: The Empty Boats Beneath the Bridge MOM-006 · Unknowing Convergence A covert MSF team descends from a bridge to inspect small night shipments requested by Drake and Sherie. The tarp-covered wooden boats arrive empty, the Drowned Choir attacks from below, and Kyrien secretly witnesses Lynleit burn the drowned hands and stand on the river. The river attack separates the team. Kyrien witnesses Lynleit's forbidden ability and keeps it secret. A Vilen river bridge linking a city street to the quarantined park Sherie and Drake ask Lynleit to assemble a loyal MSF team and investigate recurring night traffic on the Vilen river. Drake's intelligence identifies small boats moving only on the darkest nights. No operator is visible, the pattern appears intricate, and contraband remains a plausible explanation. The chosen bridge links a city street to the quarantined park. The plan requires Felix to freeze the bridge's civil safety cameras, maintain communications, and remain on the city side as fallback while the river team descends by rope, inspects the boats, and leaves by rope at the next bridge. Several nights produce no boats. Each unsuccessful watch consumes the limited camera window and exposes Lynleit or Kyrien to small oddities emerging from the quarantined park that the mission gives them no freedom to pursue. After an unsuccessful watch is formally aborted, Lynleit and Kyrien play short card games while the camera feed and bridge equipment are restored. Kyrien wins the first game through technical play, and Lynleit requests a rematch because she cannot read him. Across the failed watches, Lynleit learns that Kyrien briefly stops breathing before a risky play. Kyrien learns the small hand movement that precedes one of Lynleit's decisions. Their continued rematches and attention to each other's physical tells allow the reader to recognize attraction before either character names or prioritizes it. inferred The successful interception occurs on the fifth watch. The unsuccessful watches reveal a branch breaking before the wind reaches the trees and a pale interruption in a frozen camera feed. The boats are small wooden craft with dark tarps over shallow holds. Fixed rudders keep them aligned while the current provides most of their movement. When the boats finally appear, Reiner, Lynleit, Kyrien, Maren, and Ivo descend and find them empty. Felix remains ashore. The final card game remains unfinished when the boats appear. When an empty boat shifts, Kyrien briefly steadies Lynleit at the waist near the Sparrow holster above her tailbone. Lynleit allows the contact, and Kyrien releases her before she asks. The empty boats, drowned hands, and pale girl imply that the Drowned Choir took the contraband crews before the interception, although the surviving officers cannot prove that connection. inferred The river attack begins while the officers search the empty boats for another explanation. The officers are capable swimmers. Reaching shore becomes difficult because unseen hands seize their legs and pull downward. After reaching land, Maren describes the sensation of hands gripping and pulling her legs. Reiner, Maren, and Ivo reach the street-facing city bank with Felix's fallback line without understanding what attacked them. They do not realize that Lynleit remains behind. The hands of different sizes and states of decay suggest many drowned victims, rather than one submerged attacker. inferred Only Lynleit sees the hands clearly. They seize her most violently and drag her underwater. Lynleit wears a fitted blue suede jacket for the operation because it interferes less with ropes and wet timber than her usual coat. The hands tear the blue suede jacket away during the underwater struggle. The attack activates her childhood fear of drowning. Fury releases her blue flame at unsafe volume, and the fire catches and burns the drowned hands even beneath the water. After breaking the surface, Lynleit's palm meets resistance. She brings a knee and then both boots onto the same yielding layer until she stands above the river. The drowned hands reach upward from the darkness but cannot pass through the surface layer beneath Lynleit's feet. A pale girl emerges wearing a dress made from dead fish. Fishing line sews her eyes shut. The girl's silence and tilted head imply that a person standing on water contradicts the rule by which she takes victims. inferred Kyrien is present as Lynleit's concealed unofficial asset rather than an acknowledged MSF officer. The force in the river separates Kyrien from the official team and drives him toward the quarantined park side of the river. Kyrien reaches the park bank, enters the trees, and observes Lynleit's confrontation on the river from inside the quarantine. Only Kyrien witnesses Lynleit walking on water. Lynleit tests each step across the yielding surface and backs toward the park bank while the girl remains still. Kyrien is too careful to acknowledge what he saw and feigns innocence convincingly. Lynleit reaches the park side of the river without the jacket, where Kyrien is waiting among the trees. They remain inside the night park, drenched and struggling to catch their breath. They sit with their backs pressed together to share body heat while they recover. The contact makes each of them aware of the other's breathing through their soaked clothes, continuing the physical tell-reading established during the card games without displacing the danger of the river. Lynleit indirectly asks whether Kyrien saw anything strange during the escape. Kyrien denies seeing anything, and his careful performance of innocence gives Lynleit nothing she can safely test. Kyrien's decision to protect the secret, made without an order from Lynleit, implies the first voluntary trust inside their coerced alliance. inferred What form does the river's scar take, and in what sense does the place remember the encounter? What intelligence survives the failed operation beyond the officers' separate accounts? Does the submerged blue flame leave a lasting injury on the Drowned Choir or only force the hands to release Lynleit? The hilltop agreement gives Drake and Sherie access to a small loyal MSF team without granting them control of the agency. Their first request is a limited investigation of apparently unmanned river shipments, with contraband still the leading material explanation. Felix, Reiner, Maren, and Ivo carry an account of impossible resistance from the city bank but no shared sight of its cause. Kyrien observes the river from the quarantined trees, and Lynleit later joins him on the park bank without the blue suede jacket. Their back-to-back recovery combines the physical awareness established during the failed watches with a mutual silence around what he witnessed. Lynleit later complains about the lost jacket. Much later, after Fionn's murder, the hotel-room refuge deepens that physical trust into emotional reliance. Sherie sherie Drake drake Lynleit lynleit Felix felix Reiner reiner Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: The First Lines Back into MSF
entries.subtitle: MOM-013 · Clear Her Name
entries.text: The First Lines Back into MSF MOM-013 · Clear Her Name While Lynleit remains the target of an active arrest hunt, Kyrien helps her find secure ways to contact Felix and Reiner. Their reconnection becomes the first step in her slow campaign to reclaim MSF from Helena. Kyrien helps Lynleit reconnect with allies inside Helena's MSF. Unspecified secure contact points Lynleit remains actively hunted for arrest after escaping the immediate accusation. Kyrien helps her find ways to contact Felix and Reiner without surrendering her location. Felix and Reiner are the first trusted MSF officers brought back into her fugitive network. The renewed contact begins Lynleit's slow effort to reclaim MSF from Helena. Helena's seizure of MSF and the hunt for Lynleit leave the original handler-asset bargain without practical force. Kyrien has a real opportunity to leave the counteroffensive and chooses to remain beside Lynleit. The counteroffensive develops while Lynleit remains hunted. What secure method does Kyrien use to reach Felix and Reiner? Which officer responds first, and how does Lynleit prove the contact is genuine? What first foothold inside MSF can Felix and Reiner give her without exposing themselves? Which arresting authorities and MSF units are actively searching for Lynleit at this point? Lynleit reaches Kyrien's hotel room after exhausting her immediate escape resources. Helena's seizure has also broken the practical authority behind Lynleit's original bargain with Kyrien. Kyrien's voluntary decision to remain separates his loyalty from the coercion that began their association. The four-person link gives Lynleit an internal line into Helena's MSF and begins a prolonged contest for legitimacy, intelligence, and control under the pressure of an active manhunt. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien Felix felix Reiner reiner

entries.title: The First Missing Man
entries.subtitle: MOM-003 · Vanishing Point
entries.text: The First Missing Man MOM-003 · Vanishing Point The first man to disappear appears to be the Spill's first victim, but he independently causes the crisis. His identity and significance remain concealed for most of the story while hidden factions begin exploiting the catastrophe he created. The apparent first victim caused the Spill. Other factions begin exploiting it without the public knowing its origin. Vilen park, exact site unspecified The first missing person is a man. He is the person who causes the Spill. His identity and significance are not revealed for most of the story. He initially appears to be a victim. His role in causing the crisis remains concealed. The Spill begins independently of the hidden conspiracy and is later exploited by other actors. Other factions recognize and exploit the crisis for their own purposes. The later disappearances are caused by Holumns. Who is the man? How does he cause the Spill? Why does his identity become pivotal later? Which faction first recognizes and exploits what he caused? Who notices his disappearance first? His public identity and ordinary routine must conceal the significance he will acquire later. Holumns begin taking further victims. Investigators treat the first disappearance as the start of the case and do not know that the missing man caused the crisis.

entries.title: The Last Man out of the Park
entries.subtitle: MOM-009 · The Quarantine
entries.text: The Last Man out of the Park MOM-009 · The Quarantine A specially equipped paramilitary unit enters the sealed park and is massacred by forces it cannot understand. Captain Heyk becomes the sole survivor. Heyk loses his unit and enters Drake and Sherie's service after evacuation. The quarantined park in Vilen The park quarantine follows the disappearances of citizens, private investigators, and police officers. Police enforce the first closure before the park is sealed even from them. The government deploys specially equipped paramilitary units to investigate the whole park. The unit commanded by Captain Heyk is massacred by forces he cannot understand or explain. Heyk is the sole survivor. The Ducal Guard evacuates him briefly under Drake's orders. He is subsequently recruited into the Ducal Guard as a field agent and bodyguard serving Drake and Sherie's interests. His continuing motive is grief for the squad he lost. What does Heyk perceive during the massacre, and which parts of his account can he articulate? Why does Drake have enough warning or access to order the Ducal Guard evacuation? What evidence, equipment, or injury leaves the park with Heyk? The public already knows that people are missing. Gas, poison, or another harmful substance remains a possible explanation, although no bodies have been recovered. Heyk enters Drake and Sherie's orbit carrying grief, survivor knowledge, and direct experience that no official material explanation can fully contain. Heyk heyk Drake drake Sherie sherie

entries.title: The Nameless Street
entries.subtitle: MOM-014 · Divided Attention
entries.text: The Nameless Street MOM-014 · Divided Attention During a casual walk after lunch with Felix, Lynleit enters a deserted labyrinthine street, follows a crying girl with a red balloon, sees a dead boy below a broken fence, and is pushed from the same ledge before waking on an ordinary city bench. Lynleit returns with a memory of a dead boy that later resurfaces when she finds Fionn. Vilen old town and an untraceable street The Nameless Street is an urban myth in the old town of central Vilen. Under unknown conditions, a lost visitor may enter it alone. Its buildings and routes form a labyrinth that does not obey the surrounding city. The warning attached to the myth is not to follow anyone encountered there, because those who do may never return to ordinary streets. Days before Fionn's murder, Lynleit is walking with Felix after a work lunch when she abruptly finds herself alone, dizzy, unsteady, and suffering a severe headache. A little girl carrying a red balloon appears, loses it, and runs away crying. Lynleit catches the balloon by its thread and follows the girl's cries so she can return it. The girl eventually stands beside a broken fence above an abrupt drop, looking down at the body of a dead boy. Lynleit releases the balloon in shock. The girl smiles and pushes her from the ledge. Before reaching the ground, Lynleit wakes on a bench in the ordinary city center while Felix fans her face with a piece of paper after her apparent faint. Whether the street is a place, an illusion, or another kind of Holumn remains unresolved. When Lynleit later sees Fionn's body below the hill at the family house, the memory of the boy stupefies her and gives Helena leverage to accuse her of pushing Fionn. Felix does not explain why he accepts Lynleit's implausible account without laughing, leaving his response to be read through their long friendship. inferred What conditions admit a visitor to the Nameless Street, and why does it take Lynleit on this day? Are the girl and boy inhabitants, repeated roles, former victims, or images produced by the street? Does the fall release Lynleit, or does another interruption return her to the bench? Does the street anticipate Fionn's death, draw from Lynleit's future, or leave a pattern that later events happen to reactivate? What does Felix observe between Lynleit's last ordinary step and her collapse? Lynleit is already watching Helena study her family, but Fionn remains alive and the danger has not yet broken into an open accusation. Several days later Fionn is found below the hill at the Vilen family house. Lynleit's involuntary recognition of the dead boy gives Helena a true emotional reaction that can be assigned a false cause. Lynleit lynleit Felix felix Fionn fionn Helena helena

entries.title: The Secret Third Ally
entries.subtitle: MOM-008 · The Hidden Wager
entries.text: The Secret Third Ally MOM-008 · The Hidden Wager Lynleit eventually tells only Felix and Reiner that she has recruited Kyrien as an unknown ally and possible trump card against Helena, keeping the decision hidden even from Fionn. Reiner accepts Lynleit's decision; Felix remains opposed. Fionn is not told. Unspecified location Helena knows everyone already inside Lynleit's circle, so an unknown ally creates a favorable information imbalance. Felix and Reiner are already Lynleit's close, long-standing friends before the story begins, not subordinates who become her friends during this crisis. Lynleit eventually confines Kyrien's recruitment to Felix and Reiner and does not inform even Fionn. This is Lynleit's first deeply anti-protocol MSF decision, made with strong intuitive conviction. Fionn's assassination is still far ahead when the compartment is created. The later assassination validates Lynleit's sense of approaching danger, although it does not prove she foresaw the event itself. Felix and Reiner both regard Kyrien as a possible threat to Lynleit, especially when neither bodyguard is near her. Reiner accepts the arrangement because he chooses to trust Lynleit's judgment. Felix accepts only after Reiner's decision leaves him in the minority. Felix never fully learns to trust Kyrien and later clashes with him repeatedly. Lynleit reprimands Felix when those clashes interfere with her decision or the arrangement around Kyrien. Where and when does Lynleit disclose the compartment to Felix and Reiner? What evidence or argument does Lynleit use to justify trusting Kyrien? What continuing cover story protects the compartment from Fionn, Helena, the police, and the wider MSF? Which clash between Felix and Kyrien produces the most serious consequence for Lynleit or an operation? What would Fionn do if he learned Lynleit had hidden Kyrien from him? Lynleit has already coerced Kyrien into service after the failed assassination attempt, but the arrangement initially exists only between handler and asset. Reiner becomes the stabilizing vote that permits the compartment to continue. Felix complies without trust, creating recurring friction with Kyrien and forcing Lynleit to defend the judgment on which the entire imbalance depends. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien Felix felix Reiner reiner

entries.title: The Unresolved Assassination
entries.subtitle: MOM-007 · The Takeover
entries.text: The Unresolved Assassination MOM-007 · The Takeover Fionn is found dead below the hill at the Vilen family house after several incompatible agendas converge without one actor controlling the whole outcome. Helena knowingly opens one part of the path, then uses his death and Lynleit's stunned response to seize MSF and frame her. Fionn's death connects the hidden conflict to Helena's visible takeover. The unresolved conspiracy contains several motives, partial knowledge, and accidental cooperation, with no single clean chain of command. The hillside grounds of the Vilen family house Fionn is successfully assassinated. His body is found below the hill at the Vilen family house, but whether the fall kills him, follows another attack, or is staged remains unresolved. Lynleit's recent memory of the dead boy on the Nameless Street stupefies her when she sees Fionn below the hill. Helena assigns a false meaning to Lynleit's genuine shock and accuses her of pushing Fionn. His death creates the opening Helena uses to take control of MSF. Helena frames Lynleit for the assassination and directs a hunt for her arrest. Helena knowingly enables one part of the pressure against Fionn without understanding everything that follows. No single participant controls the complete assassination outcome. Several incompatible agendas accidentally cooperate to produce Fionn's death. The broader conflict already includes pressure from criminal Magi, foreign Magiarchates, and church actors. The unresolved issue is how each participant's intended outcome and partial action converge into the assassination. What outcome do the criminal Magi seek around Fionn? What separate outcome does a rival foreign Magiarchate seek? What separate outcome does a church faction seek? Which actions accidentally cooperate even though their authors do not share one objective? Did one faction covertly or illegally infiltrate another and use its people or resources without authorization? Does any participant's apparent affiliation conceal who truly directed them? Which door does Helena knowingly open, what does she expect to happen, and what follows beyond her knowledge? Does the fall kill Fionn, conceal another cause of death, or stage the physical evidence used against Lynleit? Manufactured political strife isolates Fionn and divides his attention while the Spill develops. Days earlier, the Nameless Street gives Lynleit an unexplained memory of a boy lying dead below a fall. Helena converts the vacancy into control of MSF, makes Lynleit the official suspect, and directs a hunt for her arrest while the true authorship remains hidden. Fionn fionn Helena helena

entries.title: The Warning Dismissed
entries.subtitle: MOM-004 · Unknowing Convergence
entries.text: The Warning Dismissed MOM-004 · Unknowing Convergence State Councillor Drake becomes convinced that a coup is developing somewhere inside Narvea, but neither his peers nor the Duke believe he has found more than disconnected irregularities. Drake cannot secure official support for his investigation. Ducal Court Drake is deeply convinced that a coup is underway. Drake holds the rank of State Councillor and has an unusually close personal relationship with the Duke. Their friendship begins when Drake is the only official willing to tell the Duke that the Duke is wrong. The Duke openly refers to Drake as a close friend and sometimes forgives his mistakes. Courtiers shun Drake as the Duke's pampered favorite and overlook that he originally earned the relationship by refusing to flatter him. He cannot yet identify where the conspiracy begins or how far it reaches. His peers ridicule the suspicion and the Duke remains skeptical. Drake interprets the park disappearances as possible cover for the illegal movement of material intended for action against Narvea or Ducal authority. What first convinces Drake that the irregularities form a coup attempt? Which peers lead the ridicule at Court? Is somebody deliberately encouraging the Court to dismiss him? Which criminal Magi, foreign Magiarchates, and church actors are shaping the conspiracy from outside Drake's field of view? Early disappearances and irregular movements need to produce the evidence that Drake reads as one political pattern. Sherie responds to her uncle's isolation by proposing contact with Lynleit outside every lawful chain of supervision. Drake drake

entries.title: Ren L17 “Sparrow”
entries.subtitle: Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm
entries.text: Ren L17 “Sparrow” Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm Ren L17 Sparrow 9×17 mm / .380 ACP Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm Small, discreet, elegant institutional pistol Standard-issued pistol for every MSF officer who has passed weapons certification. MSF purchases the Sparrow from Ren Arms and does not manufacture firearms. A slim silver-and-charcoal pistol built around the older Ren Arms metal-frame language. The brushed silver slide is elongated for its height, with a beveled nose, a long shallow ejection-port cut, a narrow rear serration block, and the RN shield set behind the caliber mark. The dark frame rises into an exposed hammer and a smooth, gently curved backstrap. Brushed silver slide over a dark charcoal frame Beveled muzzle and gently rounded upper profile Exposed serrated hammer and low conventional sights Deeply inset grip panels with broad, smooth palm surfaces Curved trigger, restrained slide controls, and no external manual safety Short extended magazine base that adds purchase without changing the narrow silhouette Despite the Sparrow's older design lineage, current-production models omit an external manual safety to reflect the demands and handling priorities of modern combat. The silver finish is standard to the firearm and is not an MSF customization. Routine issue gradually makes the ordinary Ren Arms product visually associated with MSF officers. Its small size, light visual presence, discretion, and modest chambering. lynleit Lynleit Carries the issued Sparrow as her personal sidearm. Walther PPK SIG Sauer P230 Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L19 “Magpie”
entries.subtitle: Heavier compact service pistol
entries.text: Ren L19 “Magpie” Heavier compact service pistol Ren L19 Magpie 9×19 mm Heavier compact service pistol Larger, louder, and heavier relative of the Sparrow An enlarged silver-and-charcoal development of the Sparrow for 9×19 mm. The longer brushed slide, taller dark frame, extended grip, and squared accessory profile give it more mass without abandoning the exposed hammer or the older Ren Arms silhouette. The illustration shows the optional muzzle compensator and extended magazine installed, making the pistol visibly longer in both directions than its base configuration. Brushed silver slide with a long upper relief cut Exposed serrated hammer and conventional raised sights Dark charcoal frame with the Sparrow family's curved backstrap and inset grip panels Restrained slide controls and no external manual safety Optional squared compensator with two open top ports Optional extended magazine projecting below the grip for added hand support Despite the Magpie's older design lineage, current-production models omit an external manual safety to reflect the demands and handling priorities of modern combat. Two optional attachments help the compact pistol remain controllable under the stronger recoil of its 9×19 cartridge. Attachable compensator Reduces muzzle rise and helps the shooter maintain control under the Magpie's greater recoil. Extended magazine Adds gripping surface for firmer recoil control while also increasing ammunition capacity. It fills the space between a discreet institutional pistol and a full modern duty handgun. Its close relationship to the Sparrow, with a larger, louder, heavier, and more noticeable character. SIG Sauer P230 aesthetic lineage SIG Sauer P225 / P239-type proportions Compact CZ influence Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L21 “Rook”
entries.subtitle: Micro-compact personal-defense and close-protection pistol
entries.text: Ren L21 “Rook” Micro-compact personal-defense and close-protection pistol Ren L21 Rook 9×19 mm Micro-compact personal-defense and close-protection pistol Smallest modern polymer-frame pistol in the family A common personal purchase for self-defense and a favored private sidearm among style-conscious MSF officers. Felix owns an L21 and later lends it to Lynleit when her continued reliance on the weaker 9×17 Sparrow concerns him. The Rook is a short, dense 9×19 mm pistol derived from the L24 Crow but reduced in slide, dust-cover, and grip length. Its black polymer frame and dark steel slide keep the mass low, while brass-colored details at the barrel, trigger, slide lock, and magazine release distinguish it from an ordinary service finish. Interlocking diagonal serrations at both ends of the slide give the small pistol a more intricate personal character than the Crow. Short dark steel slide over a compact black polymer frame Brass-colored barrel visible at the muzzle and through the ejection port Brass-colored trigger, slide lock, and magazine release Dense crossed serration fields at the front and rear of the slide Squared trigger guard with an undercut and a short accessory rail Extended magazine base that completes the firing grip without giving the pistol Crow-length proportions Ghost Comp is the Rook's compensated premium configuration, occupying the same conceptual place that a Spectre Comp-style model holds within a micro-compact family. The smallest modern polymer-frame 9×19 mm pistol on the Narvean market. Its size and chambering support discreet defensive carry, while its brass details and elaborate serrations make it more individual than a standard service gun. A compact, practical, intelligent bird with more confidence and modern utility than a Sparrow. felix Felix Owns an L21 as his personal sidearm. lynleit Lynleit Later carries Felix's L21 on loan when he objects to her continued reliance on the 9×17 Sparrow. Walther P22Q SIG Sauer P365 XL SIG Sauer P365 Spectre Comp Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L24 “Crow”
entries.subtitle: Standard compact law-enforcement and military secondary sidearm
entries.text: Ren L24 “Crow” Standard compact law-enforcement and military secondary sidearm Ren L24 Crow 9×19 mm Standard compact law-enforcement and military secondary sidearm Default compact state-service pistol The Crow is the preferred default secondary sidearm for Narvean law enforcement and military service. It is widely issued because it is conventional, dependable, and easy to treat as ordinary equipment rather than a specialist selection. The Crow is the compact workhorse of the modern Ren Arms family and the parent design of the smaller L21 Rook. Its dark steel slide and black polymer frame are longer and taller than the Rook, with simpler parallel serrations, a full compact grip, and neutral metal controls. The proportions remain short enough for concealed and protective work while giving the firing hand more uninterrupted surface than the micro-compact model. Dark charcoal steel slide and black polymer frame Full compact grip with a textured central panel and sculpted finger channel Straight parallel serrations at both ends of the slide Broad central slide flats with an understated caliber mark Squared undercut trigger guard and short accessory rail Neutral silver trigger and restrained controls Flush compact magazine and conventional duty sights It is the boring default of the current service family: common, dependable, and unremarkable enough to disappear into police and military equipment. Its common, capable, dark, and practical character. Glock 19 CZ P-10 C Compact modern service pistols Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L28 “Raven”
entries.subtitle: Advanced full-size law-enforcement and military service pistol
entries.text: Ren L28 “Raven” Advanced full-size law-enforcement and military service pistol Ren L28 Raven 9×19 mm Advanced full-size law-enforcement and military service pistol Performance-oriented service upgrade Police and military officers may request the Raven in place of the standard Crow when they favor better accuracy and performance. Reiner prefers the Raven. The Raven is the advanced full-size counterpart to the standard Crow. Its long dark slide carries five rounded forward windows that expose the bright barrel, while deep rear serrations, a full-length sculpted grip, and a squared frame give it greater visual weight than the Crow. A blue trigger provides the only vivid accent within an otherwise restrained service finish. Long dark-charcoal slide with broad uninterrupted side flats Five rounded forward slide windows exposing the bright barrel Deep straight rear serrations and raised conventional sights Full-size sculpted grip with finger channels and inset textured panels Squared trigger guard, extended dust cover, and accessory rail Blue trigger set against restrained black controls Flush full-size magazine and a small lanyard loop at the heel A serious performance-focused service pistol rather than a luxury model. Its barrel windows and blue trigger distinguish an officer-selected upgrade without moving it into the Swan's crafted role. A larger, darker, and more imposing service weapon than the Rook or Crow. reiner Reiner Prefers the Raven over the standard Crow for its accuracy and performance. Glock 17 Walther PDP Full Size Full-size modern service pistols Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.subtitle: Luxury long-slide pistol
entries.text: Ren L31 “Swan” Luxury long-slide pistol Ren L31 Swan 9×19 mm Luxury long-slide pistol Luxury flagship of the Ren Arms pistol family The Swan is a luxury long-slide, exposed-hammer pistol built around a 2011 and 1911-derived silhouette. A silver slide and upper frame sit over a black grip module, while the brass-colored barrel is visible through a row of elongated side windows and at the muzzle. The extended dust cover, long sight radius, skeletonized controls, flared beavertail, and sculpted frame keep the large pistol narrow and deliberate rather than bulky. Long brushed-silver slide with a row of elongated forward windows Brass-colored barrel visible through the slide and at the muzzle Black lower frame with an extended dust cover and accessory rail Exposed skeletonized hammer, long beavertail, and fitted thumb safety Lightened trigger and raised precision sights Deeply textured black grip with sculpted front and rear purchase Fine rear slide serrations and a polished script model mark A luxury sidearm outside ordinary standard issue. Its long slide, exposed mechanism, ported presentation, and mixed metal finishes give it a crafted appearance distinct from the modern duty line. Length, grace, refinement, and composure. A Raven remains a full-size duty weapon; a Swan is visibly crafted, controlled, and personal. Premium 2011 pistols Premium 1911 pistols Desert Eagle SIG GTO Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Holumns
entries.subtitle: Manifestations, effects, and evidence
entries.text: Holumns Manifestations, effects, and evidence Holumn is a category of manifestation, not a biological species. A Holumn may be a physical creature, a natural phenomenon, a repeating event, a disembodied will, or a curse. Its shape follows the fear, memory, fixation, or psychic fracture that gives it pressure. No universal weakness exists. A useful countermeasure must answer the rule expressed by the manifestation. An incident may reveal an effect without revealing the whole Holumn behind it. embodied Embodied A creature or body that occupies physical space, including forms that move without being alive. HI-003 HI-004 environmental Environmental Weather, water, terrain, or another natural system becomes the body or behavior of the manifestation. HI-003 HI-004 HI-005 event Event-bound The Holumn exists as a sequence, compulsion, rule, or occurrence with no creature that can be confronted directly. HI-002 HI-005 HI-006 disembodied Disembodied A voice, memory, desire, or will acquires agency without a stable body of its own. HI-001 curse Curse-bound A person, object, place, or action carries a hostile rule that persists until its particular condition is interrupted. HI-001 HI-002 HI-005 HI-006

entries.text: Items & Artefacts Objects, relics, and anomalous holdings Story-relevant objects, artefacts, and other nonhuman holdings that are not weapons or Holumns. IA-001 leviathan-hide-coat 2026-09-05 Leviathan-hide coat Anomalous garment Held by Lynleit A blue garment left to Lynleit through Fionn's concealed intervention. It changes form without accepting commands and shields only what Lynleit deliberately covers with it. Lynleit lynleit Fionn fionn Arranged the substitution before his death A material called the hide of leviathan The nature and source of the material are not identified. Blue coat Its familiar full-length form and the appearance in which Lynleit first understands what Fionn left her. Scarf A smaller form chosen by the garment without instruction from Lynleit. Blue suede jacket The garment can imitate the fitted jacket Lynleit lost during the Drowned Choir attack. Other clothing The coat can assume other wearable forms. Lynleit cannot choose which form appears on a given day. Minor magical protection The material can shield a covered body from minor magically induced damage and phenomena. Protection by coverage Wearing the garment is not sufficient. Lynleit must use it to cover the threatened part of her body. Protection of another person Lynleit can remove the garment and place or throw it over someone who needs immediate protection. Autonomous form The garment decides its own appearance. It does not respond to Lynleit's preference or tactical need. Protection is local to the area physically covered by the garment. The garment does not provide passive protection merely because Lynleit is wearing it. Lynleit cannot command its form or rely on it to assume the form most useful to the situation. The exact boundary of minor magically induced damage remains unknown. Arc 1 The river operation The lost jacket The Drowned Choir tears away Lynleit's fitted blue suede jacket while dragging her underwater. She later complains about losing it because she liked it. Arc 1 Middle of the main story Fionn's concealed substitution After Fionn's death, Lynleit discovers that he had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wore with the leviathan-hide garment. Arc 1 After the discovery An inherited protection Lynleit carries the garment after discovering its properties. It sometimes takes the form of the suede jacket she lost. entries.title: MSF
entries.text: MSF # msf Institutional record Known facts only World / MSF MSF Private intelligence contractor One agency, two purposes MSF is a fully private intelligence business that sells its services to the government. The initials are used publicly without a formal expansion. Fionn built a second purpose beneath its contracted work, preparing mostly ordinary people to approach threats they were never told existed. Legal status Fully private business Primary client Narvean government Headquarters Turon Full name Deliberately unrevealed 01 Dual mandate What members see depends on where they stand CONTRACTED FUNCTION Government services MSF sells intelligence, investigation, security, and operational services to the government while remaining institutionally private. FOUNDER'S DESIGN Contingency structure Fionn quietly shaped MSF so it could confront magical crises. Most members were not told that this purpose, or magic itself, existed. PERMANENT CONVERGENCE Two threat domains The Spill is never fully contained. MSF must shrink into a mainly Magi-focused task force while continuing to handle the ordinary intelligence threats it was created to confront. Father Mikhail's discovery that Lynleit has disclosed magic to Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner forces the first institutional answer to knowledge already shared. Lynleit refuses to surrender the three witnesses and instead begins moving MSF toward a partly Magi private enterprise accountable to the Magiarchy and the Church. Open the turning point → See the Church record → 02 Ownership and control The government buys access, not ownership PRIVATE GOVERNANCE Its client cannot run the company The government can negotiate contracts, purchase defined services, and decide whether to keep buying them. It has little authority over MSF's succession, command culture, internal appointments, or ordinary workings beyond the access MSF chooses to permit. MSF may also accept clients beyond the government, exposing the danger of a private contract whose obligations conflict with Narvea's interests. Government power Contract, payment, and requested scope MSF control Clients, succession, personnel, command, and internal rules POLITICAL NICKNAME “A legal mafia.” Politically savvy citizens use the joke because MSF combines private loyalty, public contracts, internal succession, and enough concentrated force to make the state uneasy, all while operating within the law. RESIDENTIAL NODE The Director's House Fionn's family residence also supports selected MSF work through its offices and library, while the formal headquarters remains in Turon. → STANDARD SIDEARM Ren L17 "Sparrow" Every MSF officer who passes weapons certification is issued the compact 9×17 pistol. MSF buys the pistol from Ren Arms and manufactures no weapons. → 03 Cryptology in plain sight Authority is worn in blue MSF · B01 ENCRYPTED M.O. A visible signal that looks ordinary Fionn built cryptology into everyday appearance. A deliberate blue garment initiates recognition, but it does not authenticate authority by itself. Top officers follow it with an innocuous challenge-response hidden inside ordinary conversation. Anyone can buy a blue coat. Only someone trusted by Fionn knows how to answer a question that sounds like small talk. Initiation Blue clothing Verification Conversational challenge-response Audience Top officers trusted by Fionn Origin Fionn's private protocol KNOWN USER Lynleit Her blue coat or jacket initiates Fionn's recognition sequence. Even while she is accused and hunted, she can complete the private exchange known to officers he personally trusted. Open Lynleit's profile → LEGITIMACY FAILURE Helena Fionn's most conservative old officers notice Helena's ignorance first. The people least inclined toward rebellion begin questioning her because strict obedience to the founder's protocol now requires disobedience toward his official successor. Open Helena's profile → 04 Command succession Fionn protects every heir by naming none MSF is a private family enterprise, and its leaders settle succession internally. Fionn deliberately refuses to identify one uncontested successor because he believes a declared heir would become an obvious target. His death divides the inheritance: Lynleit eventually becomes the new Magiarch, while Kyrien inherits the MSF director's seat during her absence. The government has little standing to settle the vacancy, and Fionn's security measure produces the succession crisis it was intended to prevent. 01 Fionn Founder without a declared heir Distributes trust through private protocols and overlapping circles, but refuses to turn any one candidate into a visible target. 02 Helena Contested inheritance Takes control after Fionn's elimination and frames Lynleit for his death. Her ignorance of his private authority protocol gradually gives influential officers reason to doubt the legitimacy of her succession. 03 Lynleit Restoration and contraction Fights to clear her name and reclaim the agency. Because the Spill cannot be fully contained, she reshapes MSF into a smaller task force centered on Magi while preserving its intelligence function. 04 Kyrien Non-Magus director in the Magiarch's absence Inherits control while Lynleit carries the Magiarchate. He must keep a private company, its government contracts, and its permanent Spill mandate functioning without magical authority or the founder's declared succession. 05 Political footprint MSF's concentration of force in Turon MSF's concentration of officers in Turon is sufficient to make a small rebellion or secession imaginable. Officer culture, divided logistics, constitutional loyalty, and the absence of any desire to rebel keep that capacity dormant. Politicians remain uneasy because the state cannot simply command or reorganize its private contractor. The final safeguard is the belief that MSF officers are decent people. See Turon in The Duchy → 06 Operational pairing A knight opens angles. A rook holds the line. ♞ KNIGHT PATTERN Felix Hacking and communications let Felix move through an operation indirectly. He finds unexpected access, redirects information, and reaches positions that a straightforward approach cannot. Open Felix's profile → ♜ ROOK PATTERN Reiner Reiner is the physically imposing brute-force specialist. He anchors protection, takes the direct route, and provides controlled power when a line must be held or broken. Open Reiner's profile → 07 Known personnel People who define the institution Founder Fionn Heir and director Lynleit Successor and rival Helena Unofficial asset, later director Kyrien Hacking and communications Felix Brute force and protection Reiner ✎ Page notes MSF Use notes to refine the agency without turning open questions into canon.

entries.title: The Church
entries.text: The Church # the-church Institutional record Known facts only World / The Church † Religious institution Knowledge kept behind doctrine Every church knows about the Magi at the highest point of its hierarchy. That knowledge descends only through controlled channels, leaving most clergy and church staff inside the same protected ignorance as the public. Public role Faith and authority Awareness Every church head Covert arm Special envoys Clergy access Highly restricted 01 Distributed knowledge The institution does not know as one body 01 MAJORITY OF THE CHURCH Ordinary faith Most clergy, staff, and worshippers operate inside the same protected ignorance as the wider public. Religious office alone does not grant access to magical knowledge. 02 HEAD OF THE HIERARCHY Guaranteed awareness The head of every church is aware of the Magi and the concealed world surrounding them. This is the stable point from which each church controls its response. 03 CONTROLLED OPERATORS Special envoys Each church maintains a contingent of operatives who carry the title of special envoy and act in the name of its head. 02 Special envoys Priesthood is the cover, not the profession OFFICIAL APPEARANCE Envoys of the heads of churches Special envoys are trained and presented as priests, allowing them to move through religious institutions with a credible public identity. Their primary training covers political operations, intelligence, combat, and covert intervention. Authority Act for a church head Cover Priesthood Structure Contingent within each church 01 Politics Institutional access, negotiation, leverage, and influence. 02 Espionage Covert placement, observation, clandestine activity, and the possible penetration of rival institutions. 03 Intelligence Collection, assessment, and controlled circulation of knowledge. 04 Combat Operational force when diplomacy and concealment fail. 05 Assassination A capability held by some envoys, not a universal assignment. 06 Specialization Each envoy develops one or several operational specialties. Separate traditions Shared purpose does not mean shared doctrine. Both traditions maintain covert, assassination-capable priesthoods while regarding the other's system as dangerously unaccountable. ORTHODOX CHURCH Trust before procedure Orthodox envoys favor personal chains of trust, confession-like secrecy, and discretionary judgment. Authority moves through relationships whose moral burden rests heavily on the person exercising it. CATHOLIC CHURCH Procedure before discretion Catholic envoys favor dossiers, compartmentalized offices, and codified authorization. Authority moves through records and separated functions intended to prevent any one operative from holding the whole design. PLAUSIBLE, NOT CONFIRMED Special-envoy capabilities make covert or illegal infiltration of Magiarchates and other factions possible. The same risk also runs in reverse, because church structures may themselves be penetrated. 03 Institutional relations Every relationship is conditional WITH THE PUBLIC Protect ignorance Magic remains outside ordinary understanding, and Church knowledge is kept narrow. WITH THE MAGIARCHY Sanction, constrain, and verify Cross-national church structures face Magiarchates that are kept territorial and separate. Both sides hunt unsanctioned Magi, but the Church often doubts that Magiarchs will act decisively enough. WITH THE STATE Reveal only what is necessary Negotiations can occur near public institutions without making their magical subject visible to ordinary officials or officers. WITH RENEGADE MAGI Hunt through special envoys Magi without a jurisdiction who practice outside church supervision or permission are treated as criminals. Special envoys pursue them alongside the resources of the responsible Magiarch. 04 Accepted boundaries Not every possible act is permitted FORBIDDEN MIRACLE-MAKING Harmless effect, prohibited form The Church distinguishes pressure-based magecraft from miracle-making that resembles wizardry or imitates acts associated with Jesus, saints, saviours, and other sacred figures. Walking on water crosses that symbolic boundary. Lynleit conceals the accidental talent because exposure would bring strong punishment even if she had harmed nobody. Open Lynleit's profile → 05 Canon doctrine Suppression doctrine THE PRACTICAL RULE Protect the boundary of public knowledge Suppression doctrine is a shared responsibility of the Church and the Magiarchy for keeping witnesses of magic from carrying dangerous knowledge back into ordinary society. The Church holds final sanction over the doctrine, while Magiarchal resources may investigate, contain, absorb, or remove witnesses under that authority. It is not one fixed punishment. The response depends on what the witness knows, how credible they are, how much exposure has already occurred, and whether the witness can be contained without creating a larger crisis. 01 · IRREVERSIBLE Elimination Murder, assassination, or kidnapping may be considered when the Church believes exposure cannot be contained by other means. 02 · PRESSURE Coercion Extortion, intimidation, bribery, and threats can redirect a witness without making the magical truth public. 03 · REFRAME Discrediting A witness may be framed as mentally ill, unreliable, or otherwise incapable of persuading anyone who hears the account. 04 · ABSORPTION Church integration Some witnesses are forced into Church staff or clergy, where their access, movement, and story can be controlled from inside the institution. 05 · SERVICE Magiarchal integration Others may be absorbed into Magiarchy service staff or a supervised operational role, turning dangerous knowledge into a controlled obligation under Church-sanctioned authority. UNRESOLVED BOUNDARY Suppression can include coercion, forced service, or killing. Church sanction does not settle disagreements over whether a particular witness must be silenced. 06 Story contact Father Mikhail finds the first witness breach Early in September, Fionn and Lynleit enter a church for confidential negotiations while Felix and Reiner wait outside. Later, Father Mikhail becomes the first authority to discover that Lynleit has disclosed forbidden knowledge to Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner. When she insists on handling the breach herself, he warns her: “What you do is none of my business, but don't be surprised if I'll be sent to clean up your mess.” The confrontation begins the pressure to place part of MSF under Magiarchal and Church accountability. Open the confrontation → Meet Father Mikhail → ✎ Page notes The Church Use notes to define doctrine, hierarchy, and boundaries without treating open questions as facts.

entries.title: The Director's House
entries.text: The Director's House # director-house Residential location record Family home · discreet MSF node World / The Director's House Residence · family seat · operational node A family home with institutional gravity The family keeps two houses. The original stands in Turon, where Lynleit lived with her mother during junior school. After her mother's death, Fionn moved the family to Vilen for better access to the capital. The Vilen house is a three-floor residence whose offices, library, and discreet working rooms also support MSF operations. Floors Three Family houses Turon and Vilen Setting Vilen hillside above the river Rear grounds Small park and garden Operational role Residential mini-HQ 01 Family history Two houses, one family history Distant city House on the hill Rear garden City river Behind the house, a compact private park descends toward the river-facing edge of the hill. Thick vegetation and mature trees surround the residence closely enough for wind in the leaves and branches to remain part of its daily sound. Below, the river flows toward Vilen's city center. Lynleit regards flowing water as life energy: its movement gives her emotional grounding even though she has feared drowning since childhood. 02 Vertical plan Three floors, three degrees of distance 03 Highest floor Lynleit's chosen room A desk between trees and water After the family moved from Turon to Vilen, Lynleit made a third-floor study-bedroom her condition for accepting the new house. Its height lets her look beyond the trees toward the river while she works. Wind moving through leaves and branches gives the room the natural sound she finds most inspiring. 02 Private interior Family domain The quieter center of the house The second floor contains the family's private rooms. 01 Garden level Glass and greenery Glass-enclosed rooms The rear side of the first floor opens into glass-enclosed relaxation areas facing dense greenery. In summer they extend domestic life among the trees. In winter the same rooms preserve the sight and sound of the landscape while protecting everyone inside from cold, rain, and wind. READING Library A substantial domestic library supports study, research, and the quieter habits of a family whose private responsibilities extend beyond the household. WORK Several offices Multiple offices allow private meetings and administrative work to occur without converting the entire residence into an overt agency building. OPEN DETAIL Exact allocation The floor-by-floor placement of the library, offices, service rooms, and other bedrooms remains intentionally undefined. 03 Dual role Residence and command space occupy the same address FAMILY NEST A place that belongs to the family first Bedrooms, study, reading, the garden, and the glass relaxation rooms give the house a genuine domestic identity. It stores ordinary memories alongside the pressures attached to Fionn's position. SHARED THRESHOLD Privacy becomes operational access The director can receive trusted people, review sensitive work, and continue agency business without leaving the protection and familiarity of home. MINI-HQ A discreet extension of MSF The offices and library support selected meetings, planning, and confidential work. MSF's formal headquarters remains in Turon. 04 Story connections Events at the house RESIDENT Lynleit Her third-floor room brings together the distant view, surrounding trees, and flowing water she uses for inspiration and emotional grounding. → DIRECTOR Fionn His public family seat also supports the confidential demands of MSF leadership. → INSTITUTION MSF The house is a residential operational node, distinct from the agency's formal headquarters in Turon. → EARLY OMEN Ash enters the house The grey trespasser turns the protected family interior into a comic warning, then stays as a permanent resident. → ✎ Page notes House Use notes to refine rooms, access, and domestic details without turning open architecture into canon.

entries.title: The Duchy
entries.text: The Duchy # narvea National reference record Country profile World / The Duchy of Narvea COUNTRY RECORD NAR · 001 Primary setting The Duchy of Narvea A large, sovereign Baltic country built around two sources of legitimacy: the Ducal Crown and the parliamentary state. Sovereignty resides jointly in the Crown and the Nation. Government Constitutional duchy State identity Multinational and civic Parliamentary capital Vilen Ducal seat Rennel MSF headquarters Turon Region Eastern Baltic Story role Main country Diplomatic role European meeting ground Jump to Territory Cities Authority Diplomacy Institutions Culture 01 Territory A state along the eastern Baltic Narvea reaches from the approaches to St. Petersburg toward the southwestern Baltic frontier near Gdansk. National flag Ducal standard Show details for Rennel Show details for Turon Show details for Bird's Nest Show details for Port City Show details for Vilen Map of Narvea Hover, focus, tap, or select a city Mapped roles Why these cities matter Five centers divide Narvea's political, diplomatic, and strategic life. 01 Rennel · Ducal seat Home of the Crown, Court, ceremony, and dynastic archives. It represents continuity and sovereign legitimacy. 02 Turon · MSF headquarters The private contractor's concentration of officers gives it unusual local power. Constitutional loyalty and divided logistics restrain it, but politicians know the final safeguard is the officers' own decency. 03 Bird's Nest · Diplomatic ground Rival nations meet here to negotiate. Every country uses a different name for the city. 04 Port City · Western gateway Narvea's principal western connection to Baltic trade, maritime movement, and foreign access. 05 Vilen · Parliamentary capital Parliament, Cabinet, ministries, courts, and financial institutions make it the center of the modern state. 02 Dual capital tradition One country, two political worlds Rennel is the Ducal capital, Vilen the governmental capital, and Turon the military center and home of MSF. Rennel City image unavailable THE CROWN Ducal capital Rennel Located in the old Narva region. It represents dynasty, continuity, military tradition, nobility, and ceremony. Ducal Palace and Court Privy Council Ducal Guard headquarters Dynastic and heraldic archives Formal audiences Vilen City image unavailable THE STATE Parliamentary capital Vilen Narvea's center of government, law, administration, commerce, and modern political life. Its enormous urban park becomes the first visible center of the disappearances. Parliament and Cabinet Government ministries Major courts Financial institutions Vast park at the center of the first disappearances Turon City image unavailable THE PRESSURE POINT MSF headquarters Turon Turon is home to the headquarters of MSF, a fully private intelligence business that sells services to the government while retaining control of its own succession and internal affairs. Its officers give the company enough local force to mount a small rebellion or attempt secession if it ever chose to do so. Officer culture, divided logistics, constitutional loyalty, and a genuine lack of separatist ambition keep that possibility theoretical. MSF headquarters and senior officer corps Operational strength beyond ordinary agency needs Potential leverage over the central government Political anxiety that ultimately depends on personal restraint No rebellion is openly planned. The possibility simply remains in the backrooms of Narvean political life, where senior officials cannot afford to ignore it. 03 Constitutional balance Parliament governs. The Crown safeguards. Parliament chooses and controls the government, passes laws, and authorizes public money. The Duke gives constitutional form to those decisions and intervenes only through narrowly defined reserve powers. C Ducal sphere The Duke Head of state and constitutional guardian. Formally appoints the Prime Minister who commands parliamentary confidence Promulgates laws already passed by Parliament without rewriting them Represents the state, receives ambassadors, and maintains the Court and Ducal Guard Uses narrow reserve powers only during constitutional emergencies CROWN CONSTITUTIONAL BALANCE NATION P Democratic sphere Parliament & Government Elected authority and the executive accountable to it. Parliament grants or withdraws confidence in the Prime Minister and government Parliament debates, amends, and passes laws and approves taxation and spending The Prime Minister directs Cabinet, ministries, and the civil service The government sets domestic, defence, economic, social, and ordinary foreign policy 04 Diplomatic tradition The room where Europe stepped back Narvea became a trusted meeting ground where opposing European powers could settle their differences before rivalry became open conflict. NEUTRAL GROUND Authority meets here before force. Narvea's influence rests less on commanding Europe than on keeping its rivals in the same room long enough to avoid escalation. Method Conference and settlement Legacy Borders shaped without continental war 1803 to 1815 NAPOLEONIC WARS Narvea helped contain a continental crisis Its mediation played an important and constructive role during the wars. The settlements of this period also began shaping Narvea's borders into their modern form. 1917 EASTERN SETTLEMENT Revolution was prevented Opposing powers gathered in Narvea and contained an eastern political crisis before it could become a revolution. 1939 CONTINENTAL SETTLEMENT Europe avoided a major war Another Narvean conference stopped escalation between European powers, allowing the continent's borders and history to take a different course. NOW LIVING LEGACY Diplomacy became ordinary culture The habit of mediation still shapes how Narvean institutions understand authority, legitimacy, and public service. LANGUAGE AS CIVIC PRACTICE Multilingualism is expected, not exceptional. People in authority are expected to know several languages, but the custom reaches far beyond diplomatic circles. Narveans often move between languages in ordinary conversation for precision, courtesy, emphasis, or simple habit, even when no negotiation is taking place. THE CITY WITH MANY NAMES Bird's Nest is only one of its titles. Most negotiations between rival nations take place in this city. Every country calls it something different, carrying its own name for the same diplomatic ground. Bird's Nest is the Narvean title, and its unusual sound reflects the city's role as the place where competing powers gather without fully belonging to one another. 05 Institutions Parallel systems, one state Responsibility is divided deliberately. Similar-looking institutions can answer to different centers of authority. STATE · 01 Narvean Armed Forces The national Army, Navy, Air Force, reserves, and intelligence services answer through the constitutional government. National defence CROWN · 01 Ducal Guard An elite Crown formation protecting the ducal family, residences, and selected constitutional institutions. Dynastic security STATE · 02 Narvean Police Ordinary law enforcement remains under civilian authority, most likely through the Ministry of the Interior. Public order CROWN · 02 Privy Council Advises the Duke on constitutional questions, appointments, security, foreign affairs, and emergencies. Sovereign counsel BRIDGE · 01 Council of State A standing bridge between Crown and government for constitutional review, administrative law, major appointments, disputes, and emergency continuity. Its most dangerous cases begin when ordinary state sovereignty collides with supernatural authority the public constitution cannot acknowledge. Jurisdictional paradox Service and precedence Rank is not the same as office Narvea maintains its own hierarchy of court and civil ranks. A person's rank controls formal precedence, while their actual work may be diplomatic, judicial, academic, military, or administrative. 01 Chancellor of Narvea 02 Actual Privy Councillor 03 Privy Councillor 04 Actual State Councillor 05 State Councillor Drake's rank 06 Collegiate Councillor RANK AND OFFICE Drake is a State Councillor by rank and an Official for Special Assignments by office. He serves as an elite executive troubleshooter attached to a high-ranking personal office. Free from routine administration, he carries delegated authority into confidential criminal investigations, political counter-espionage, emergency corruption audits, and diplomatic errands. Open Drake's profile → 06 Cultural character Layered, regional, distinctly Narvean Narvean is a shared political identity, not a single ethnicity. Different regions keep their own language, faith, architecture, and historical memory. CIVIC IDENTITY The state is the common ground. Regional, linguistic, religious, urban, and rural communities can all be fully Narvean. INSTITUTIONS Old military customs, ducal administration, civic government, and modern Narvean constitutionalism. FAITH Catholic and Orthodox traditions coexist across different regions. PUBLIC LIFE Baltic merchant culture, old aristocratic ceremony, and modern parliamentary politics. CENTRAL TENSION A modern country that never fully discarded inherited hierarchy. Why it matters to the story Narvea is stable because old and modern power remain in balance. It is also vulnerable for the same reason. Every crisis can become a dispute over who has the right to act, what must remain hidden, and which institution will bear the consequences. entries.title: The Magiarchy
entries.text: The Magiarchy # the-magiarchy Magical governance framework Territorial order World / The Magiarchy Territorial magical order A hierarchy that ends at the border The highest official position a Magus can obtain is Magiarch. Each Magiarch oversees magical affairs and relations with the churches inside a defined territory, but no Magiarch may turn that authority into a larger united organization. Highest office Magiarch Jurisdiction One territory Primary relation Magiarchy and churches Higher union Explicitly forbidden 01 Highest office The Magiarch is the ceiling of lawful magical authority OFFICIAL APEX Magiarch The office is usually held by the main Magus assigned to oversee the Magiarchy within a single territorial jurisdiction. 01 Territorial oversight Each Magiarch holds authority within a defined country or district. No universal magical hierarchy exists above them. 02 Church relations The office manages the local relationship between organized Magi and the churches that monitor and counterbalance them. 03 Factional leadership A Magiarch and the Magi aligned with them become a political actor with interests, allies, rivals, and local pressures. RECOGNITION PROCESS Authority is requested, judged, or won Several methods are known, and some carry far more respect than others. 01 Formal application A Magus with a substantial network, friendships, and connections submits a claim to the Church. Church approval gives the office its ordinary seal of legitimacy. 02 Contested decision When several candidates possess credible claims, church authorities and respected Magiarchs from other jurisdictions may share the decision. 03 Fitness contest A deadlock may be settled through a duel or another controlled competition intended to measure fitness for the office. 04 Sanctioned war The radical path permits rival Magi to fight to the death under Church supervision. Innocents cannot be harmed, and the existence of magic must remain hidden from the wider world. RECOGNITION CAN BE WITHDRAWN The Church may revoke recognition and destroy a Magiarch's legitimacy, but it cannot directly install a replacement. The office is independent enough to deny the Church a power of appointment, yet dependent enough that Church disapproval can create a vacancy nobody is automatically empowered to solve. 02 Territorial scale Jurisdiction follows practical size COMMON MODEL One country A single Magiarch may oversee the whole territory when its size and magical population can be managed as one jurisdiction. LARGER TERRITORY One district A large country may be divided into several Magiarchates. Each governs its own district independently, with no national magical superior. WHO DRAWS THE LINE Church authorities certify Magiarchate boundaries according to practical governability. The same transnational religious hierarchy that prevents Magi from forming a transnational command therefore decides where each supposedly independent magical jurisdiction begins and ends. 03 Structural counterbalance Magiarchal power is fragmented because the churches are not MAGIARCHATES Territorial and separate Magiarchs are explicitly forbidden from uniting into a larger organization. Their lawful authority stops with their territory. COUNTERWEIGHT CHURCHES Organized across borders The churches retain cross-national organization, giving them a wider structure that counterbalances the concentrated power of Magi. WHY THE BAN EXISTS A united organization of Magiarchs would overturn the intended balance and create open conflict with the churches. Examine the church counterweight → 04 Relations without a sovereign Magiarchates exist in an anarchic order NO HIGHER MAGICAL GOVERNMENT There is no lawful authority above the Magiarchs capable of reliably settling disputes between them. Anarchy here does not mean constant chaos. It means the absence of a superior power that can compel every Magiarchate to obey. 01 Self-preservation Each faction must judge threats and protect its own position. 02 Alliance Cooperation depends on interest, trust, and temporary alignment. 03 Rivalry Competing aims can produce pressure resembling conflict between states. 04 Uncertainty No Magiarch can be certain how another faction will use its power. PLAUSIBLE METHOD · NOT CONFIRMED Institutions may penetrate one another Rival Magiarchates, criminal Magi, and church networks may covertly or illegally place operatives, informants, or influence inside one another's structures. If this occurs, visible affiliation cannot be treated as proof of who truly directed an action. 05 Outside the sanctioned order A Magus without jurisdiction becomes a common enemy CRIMINAL STATUS Unbound and unsanctioned A Magus is treated as a criminal when they belong to no territorial jurisdiction and practice outside church supervision or permission. 01 No jurisdiction The Magus does not belong to a recognized Magiarchate. 02 No church sanction Their practice proceeds without church supervision or permission. CHURCH RESPONSE Special envoys The churches use their covert operatives to identify, pursue, and suppress Magi outside the sanctioned order. Examine special envoys → SHARED TARGET MAGIARCH RESPONSE Territorial resources The responsible Magiarch is expected to use the resources under their authority to hunt the same offender. SUPPRESSION DOCTRINE Witness control is a shared responsibility of the Church and Magiarchy, but the Church holds final sanction. Magiarchal resources may carry out coercion, discrediting, forced service, kidnapping, or lethal removal according to circumstance and perceived exposure. Read the doctrine record → UNEASY COOPERATION The pursuit is shared, but trust is not. Church authorities often doubt that a Magiarch will act decisively enough against another Magus. 06 Succession after Fionn The Magiarchate passes to Lynleit NARVEA Lynleit After Fionn 's death, his biological daughter eventually inherits the Magiarchate as Narvea's new Magiarch. While that office keeps her away from MSF, Kyrien carries the directorate in her absence. The two heirs divide the offices Fionn once held together. Open Lynleit's profile → Open the MSF record → Awaiting definition Open framework questions Who convenes a replacement process after recognition is withdrawn Rules for duels, fitness contests, and sanctioned wars How contested boundary revisions are appealed What customs govern disputes between Magiarchates ✎ Page notes Magiarchy Use notes to define offices and inter-Magiarchate customs without turning open questions into canon.
